  "text": "On Saturday, Martin went to his father's flat to collect the kitchen table. The new tenant was moving in on Monday.

His sister had left the keys with the neighbour, who handed them over in an envelope.

“There’s a little one for the meter cupboard,” she said.

Inside, the rooms smelled of carpet cleaner. Without the chairs, the table looked larger than he remembered. He set his toolbox on it, then moved it to the floor.

The first three legs came off easily. The fourth had a different bolt.

His father had always repaired things with whatever was available. Martin could hear himself complaining about it, years ago, while they struggled to hang a door.

He tried two spanners before finding one that fitted.

Under the tabletop was a square of masking tape. Written on it in pencil were his sister’s name and a date from twenty years earlier.

He rang her.

“Did Dad promise you the table?”

“No. Why?”

He described the label.

There was a pause.

“That’ll be when I borrowed it for the school fair. He labelled everything. Even the extension lead.”

“Right,” Martin said.

“Have you got the leg off?”

“Nearly.”

He put the phone down and worked the bolt loose. A thin fall of sawdust landed on his trousers.

Before carrying the top downstairs, he peeled away the tape. It tore across the date, leaving his sister’s name intact.

He stood with the scrap stuck to his thumb. Then he pressed it back underneath, smoothing it firmly so it would stay."
